topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic and frames the study of the complement system.

topics.label: Principles and core mechanics of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational framework of the complement cascade, including its overall purpose, naming rules, and the central role of C3 activation.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how the alternative, lectin, and classical recognition pathways activate complement on pathogen surfaces to reach a trigger threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the downstream biological actions triggered by complement activation to destroy pathogens and stimulate inflammation.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the regulatory proteins and inhibitory mechanisms that protect host cells from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the clinical manifestations, autoimmune risks, and susceptibility to specific infections resulting from deficiencies in individual complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen strategies for complement evasion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic discusses the molecular mechanisms evolved by pathogens, exemplified by Staphylococcus aureus, to circumvent complement-mediated killing.

topics.label: Lecture closing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture on complement and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
